newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW - Regalian sees strong Asia sales.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Regalian sees strong Asia sales.

text.p: London developer Regalian Properties PLC sees Asian sales contributing about half of its total sales for 1997, chairman and chief executive David Goldstone said on Wednesday.

While declining to give any profit forecasts for the financial year ending April 1997, he said analysts' forecast of a net profit of 3.9 million stg in 1997, up 250 percent from last year's 1.6 million stg, was "not unreasonable".
Goldstone, in Singapore to launch a new project, said the group has a development programme of more than 200 million stg to be sold over the next two-and-a-half years.
"About 40 percent of sales would be from the Far East," he said.
Regalian has sold about 40 million stg worth of property through its Singapore office and 20 million stg through its Hong Kong office since they were set up last year in May.
"We actually bring developments to Singapore before we sell them in London because there is more appetite here for buying in advance," said Goldstone.
Typically, buyers in Singapore and Hong Kong buy the property after looking at plans and than wait for about two years for their homes to be built, he said.
The typical British purchaser normally does not like to buy property which has not been built, he added.
Separately, Regalian will be holding talks with local developers interested in entering the London property market, said Goldstone.
He added that the London property market was looking upbeat and he expects home prices to rise about 10 percent this year after rising some 10 percent last year.
